science.title: Fuzzy relation-aware graph role clustering for sentiment-augmented fake news detection
science.description: Existing research on fake news detection shows that sentiment information in social media comments can provide important clues for judging the authenticity of news. However, existing sentiment enhancement methods usually treat comments as independent samples and mainly rely on the semantic representation and sentiment features of individual comments for role clustering, ignoring the potential relationship structure between comments. In fact, the user roles in the comment section are not entirely determined by the sentiment polarity of individual comments. Comments expressing the same negative sentiment may come from blind followers, skeptics, or debunkers. To address this issue, we propose a fuzzy relation-aware graph role clustering framework, FRGC. Specifically, FRGC models comments under the same news event as nodes and constructs an event-level comment graph based on semantic similarity to capture latent comment relations beyond individual representations. It further introduces sentiment probability distributions and their uncertainty to calibrate semantic edge weights, avoiding the direct use of unreliable sentiment polarity for relation modeling. Through this design, sentiment information is incorporated as an uncertain auxiliary signal while preserving the dominance of semantic relations. Furthermore, a graph encoder layer and a weak graph regularization term are introduced to obtain relation-enhanced comment representations and improve the stability of latent role clustering. Experimental results on multiple datasets validate the effectiveness of FRGC. Specifically, FRGC achieves an F1-score of 97.1 on Weibo-comp and obtains a Macro-F1 of 36.5 and RMSE of 74.3 on RumourEval-19, outperforming existing methods and demonstrating the effectiveness of fuzzy relation-aware graph modeling for sentiment-enhanced fake news detection.

science.title: Machine learning based distribution mapping of gold in soil samples using aqua regia digestion and solid phase extraction
science.description: In the present work, aqua regia followed by solid phase extraction using activated carbon was developed for soil sample treatment. The analytical approach was further integrated with machine learning algorithms enabling the prediction of gold potential zone. Some modifications such as roasting the samples and hydrofluoric acid addition for silicon structure removal of the samples have also been investigated. The analytical performance of the method was evaluated via certified reference materials and geological samples, at different concentration levels. Random Forest, Gaussian Process Regression and Ordinary Kriging models were subsequently used considering nonlinear spatial relationships, uncertainty prediction and generate predictive gold distribution map. Despite the significant effect of sample roasting, HF addition had only a minor and negligible effect (according to t-test at 95% confidence level) and the proposed method was able to detect gold concentrations ranging from 18.0 ng/g to 53,000 ng/g in soil samples and down to 0.01 µg/mL in aqueous samples with correlation coefficients greater than 0.9991. The method accuracy and precision were in the range of 3.7–9.6 and − 9.5-+7.4, respectively. Comparison of responses obtained for the analysis of 40 different geological samples via fire assay and aqua regia digestion shows a good compatibility which verified the aqua regia as a simple, low cost and reliable treatment technique.
